title: Lightweight request instrumentation & streaming propagation gateway
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Our current SDK middleware and edge proxies add non-trivial overhead when normalizing trace context for streaming protocols (gRPC bidi streams, WebSocket, server-sent events). We see inconsistent propagation across protocol upgrades and high allocations when unpacking rich OTLP/B3 headers on hot request paths. This causes noisy sampling, orphan spans, and makes per-request cost unclear.

Goal: Implement a compact, forward-compatible propagation gateway and low-allocation SDK hooks that: 1) provide a single stable envelope for cross-protocol context (HTTP/1.x, HTTP/2, gRPC, WS), 2) preserve sampling signals and parent linkage in a tiny header, 3) run with <30 microseconds median overhead on hot paths, and 4) are opt-in behind an enablement flag with phased rollout.

Constraints and non-goals: This ticket does not replace full OTEL header support; it provides a minimal fallback envelope for high-throughput paths and streaming edge cases. We must not change public API semantics for hosted customers without release notes; default disabled for enterprise private until security review is complete.

Design highlights: Introduce a streaming propagation gateway (runtime component) that accepts native headers and emits a compact header named 'x-rw-ctx' with a stable 24-byte binary envelope base64-encoded. Envelope contents: trace-id (16 bytes), parent-id (4 bytes), sampling-priority (1 byte), protocol-flags (1 byte), version (1 byte), crc (1 byte). SDK hooks will parse this envelope with zero-allocation fast path and attach a lightweight request token for local span attribution. Edge proxy will normalise incoming B3/W3C/OTEL headers into x-rw-ctx for downstream consumers. Sampling decisions: support edge-hint and local-override with a controlled priority field to allow customers to mark high-customer-impact requests for prioritized sampling.

Performance: implement a branchless parsing path in the SDK using slice views and prefetch-friendly parsing, and a fallback slow path for clients that need full OTEL decoding. Build a microbenchmark harness (bench/request_hook) and target median overhead <30us, p99 <200us at 95th percentile under contention.

Compatibility: Gateway supports translation both ways (B3 -> x-rw-ctx -> W3C) and exposes an escape hatch header 'x-rw-ctx-full' when full OTEL baggage is present (disabled by default).

Rollout: Canary on 10% of production hosts for 48 hours with auto-rollback criteria (increase in orphan spans >1.5x or request latency p95 increase >5%).

Deliverables: SDK patches (node/python/go/rust), runtime proxy change, runtime config toggle, docs and migration guide, test harness, dashboard for rollout metrics.
acceptance_criteria: Edge proxy normalizes B3/W3C/OTEL into x-rw-ctx on HTTP/gRPC/WS in correctness tests
SDK zero-allocation parse path implemented for at least Node and Go; microbench added
Bench target: median overhead <30us and p99 <200us under simulated production load
Canary rollout automation and rollback triggers implemented
Migration doc and console flag added; security review completed and mitigations documented
implementation_steps: Draft envelope binary layout and versioning doc (RFC) and share with infra+security
Add runtime component: propagation gateway that normalizes headers (HTTP/gRPC/ws)
Implement SDK fast-path parser (Node, Go) and slow-path OTEL parser as fallback
Build microbenchmark harness and perf dashboard (bench/request_hook)
Integrate canary rollout with infra autoscaler and rollout controller
Add migration guide, console toggle, and telemetry to track sampling & orphan spans
Run security review and update RFC with encryption/attestation notes if required
Ship canary, monitor for rollback criteria, expand rollout if green
